links.targetTitle: The 90% Encumbrance Ratio cap is a commitment by Grove Devel

title: Stablewatch operates the Osero Liquidity Layer and commits to an Encumbrance Ratio at or below 90%
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.1.3.1 reads: "Stablewatch will operate the Osero Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio," referencing A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 for the ratio's definition.

Two facts are established in one sentence. Stablewatch — introduced at A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1.3.1.1.6 merely as "a development company that provides services to the Osero Foundation" — is also the operator of the liquidity layer. And the encumbrance commitment is *its* commitment, phrased as an agreement by a named private company inside a governance document.

That placement matters. The Agent is an Atlas construct and cannot bear obligations the way a company can; naming the operator as the promisor makes the undertaking attributable to an entity that can be held to it. It also means the commitment survives changes in Osero's governance — it is not something OSERO holders granted and could revoke.

The concentration is worth flagging. The same company builds the system (for the Foundation), operates it, and gives the risk undertaking about how it will be run — with the Freezer Multisig and the Core Operator Relayer Multisig, both outside Stablewatch's control, as the structural counterweights.

A 90% ceiling is also a high ceiling. It leaves 10% headroom against the encumbrance measure, so the commitment is a limit on the tail rather than a conservative operating target.
description: The risk undertaking is given by the development company running the system, not by the Agent or its Foundation, and is written into the Atlas as a named commitment.
